notes: Directus bootstraps the database on its first start and creates the first administrator from ADMIN_EMAIL (the email entered at create time) and the generated ADMIN_PASSWORD. Later starts keep the existing users and password.

Directus 12 runs on the free Core tier without a licence key. SSO, custom permission rules and custom LLM connections need a Directus licence (free for organisations under $5M revenue and 50 employees).

The official example adds Redis for caching; it is left out because caching is off by default, which keeps the stack to the app and PostgreSQL. Plain PostgreSQL 17.11 replaces the example's PostGIS image; geometry fields need PostGIS.
PUBLIC_URL is the URL key. IP_TRUST_PROXY keeps the Directus 12 default (false), so activity logs record the proxy address rather than a header the client could forge.
Uploads and extensions live in their own named volumes; PostgreSQL has its own volume and no published port. Email (password resets, invitations) needs EMAIL_* settings that are not configured.

The healthcheck uses 127.0.0.1, not localhost: BusyBox wget in the image resolves localhost to ::1 first and Directus listens on IPv4 only, so a localhost probe was refused and the container stayed unhealthy (found live, RC-25).
The 1g application floor fits Directus's Node process with headroom for imports; the database uses the panel database-memory default.
Verified live on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (RC-25): created from the 1-Click Recipes tab, Running, HTTPS, first login and a real-use check passed; every image ref below is in its tested list.
